Write ONE test file: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server-persistence.test.mjs (node:test + node:assert/strict, Node built-ins only). Do NOT edit server.mjs, public/*, or test/helpers/*. Skills: load `tdd-workflow` if available (optional).

Context: spec (source of truth) at /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/spec.md ("Server" section). Server: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs (read only). Data layout note: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/backend-api.md (layout `{"nextId":N,"bookings":[...]}`). Harness: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/helpers/server-harness.mjs (read it): `makeTempDir`, `removeDir`, `startServer({env, cwd})` → {port, output, isRunning, stop} (PORT '0' by default), `request(port,{method,path,headers,body})` (body may be string/Buffer/array of chunks for chunked), `postBooking(port, obj, {contentType, raw})`, `validBooking(overrides)`, `JSON_TYPE`. Always spawn with cwd = fresh temp dir and an explicit DATA_FILE inside it; stop servers and remove dirs in after/finally.

Project rules: functions <50 lines, no console.log, exact equality (deepEqual whole values), every spec value asserted exactly.

Tests:
1. No write at startup or on non-changing requests: write a valid data file by hand in the server layout but with unusual formatting (e.g. compact one-line JSON with one booking `{"nextId":5,"bookings":[{"id":3,"room":"Borealis","title":"Plan","date":"2026-11-04","start":"13:00","end":"14:00"}]}`), set its mtime to a fixed past time with fs.utimes. Start; do GET /api/rooms, GET /api/bookings, GET /api/bookings?date=2026-11-04, GET /, GET /app.js, a 404, a 405, a POST that fails with 400, a POST that fails with 409 (overlap with booking 3), a POST with 415, a DELETE of a missing id (404). Afterwards the file bytes are identical and mtime unchanged. Also GET /api/bookings returns that booking exactly; the next POST gets id 5.
2. ENOENT start writes nothing: DATA_FILE='data.json' missing; after startup + GETs the file still does not exist; after a successful POST it exists.
3. Persistence across restart: POST three bookings (ids 1,2,3), DELETE 3 (the highest) and 1, stop, restart same DATA_FILE: GET /api/bookings deepEquals the same list as before restart; next POST gets id 4 (ids never reused, even after deleting the highest id). Do a second restart cycle to confirm id 5 next.
4. Every change saved before reply: right after a 201 reply (before stopping), read the data file and parse — it contains the new booking; right after a 204 DELETE reply, the file no longer contains it. (Do not depend on layout beyond the backend note: check `bookings` array contents and `nextId`.)
5. Save failure: DATA_FILE='sub/data.json' with folder sub created; start; POST A → 201 id 1. Remove the folder sub recursively. POST B (non-overlapping) → status 500, Content-Type exactly 'application/json; charset=utf-8', body deepEqual {error:'internal error'}. DELETE /api/bookings/1 → 500 {error:'internal error'}. GET /api/bookings → still exactly [A with id 1] (nothing changed). The server is still running (isRunning() true) and the folder 'sub' was not recreated by the server. Recreate 'sub'; POST B → 201 with id 2 (next id not consumed by the failed save). DELETE 1 → 204.
6. Concurrency: 12 overlapping POSTs (same room/date, varied but all-overlapping times, e.g. 09:00-10:00 .. with start '09:0X' end '10:00') sent at once with Promise.all → exactly one 201, eleven 409; GET shows exactly one booking. Then 15 non-overlapping concurrent POSTs (distinct start hours or rooms) → all 201, ids unique and equal the set {2..16}. After restart the list is the same 16 bookings and next id is 17.
7. Large bodies still get replies (the server reads the whole body first): with a 2 MB body: POST /api/bookings with Content-Type text/plain → 415 {error:'content type must be application/json'}; POST /api/bookings with application/json → 413 {error:'body too large'}; POST /nope → 404 {error:'not found'}; PUT /api/rooms → 405 {error:'method not allowed'}; DELETE /api/bookings/1 with a 2 MB body → 404 {error:'booking not found'}. Also the same 413 using a chunked body (array of 64 KB Buffer chunks totalling 1 MB, no Content-Length). Each must resolve without ECONNRESET/EPIPE.
8. After an aborted request (client destroys socket mid-body: use http.request with Content-Length 100000, write 10 bytes, then req.destroy()), the server keeps running and still answers GET /api/rooms 200.

Run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 && node --test test/server-persistence.test.mjs` until it passes against the real server. If a test fails because the SERVER seems to violate the spec, don't change the server or weaken the test; report it (test, expected, actual). Report: file path, test count, pass/fail summary, suspected spec violations.

content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from user) — owner: supervisor — 2026-11-02 2 3 AUTOMATED BENCHMARK TASK. No human will answer questions: the requirements below are complete and final. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. The project's own tests must pass at the end. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. **Failing test:** "large bodies still get their replies".
- **Expected:** every large-body request gets its reply (415, 413, 404, 405, 404, then the chunked 413) with no connection error.
- **Actual:** one of the six requests rejects with `read ECONNRESET`. The error doesn't say which one, because the test sends them one after another and doesn't label them.

- **Possible cause:** the reset could be the server's behaviour or a client-side quirk of sending a 2 MB body to a server that replies. I can't tell which without isolating the case.
- **Spec violation?** I can't say for sure. If it reproduces, I'd treat it as a suspected violation of the spec line "Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body... so the client always receives the reply."

**What I need:** permission to use Bash again. Then I'd run the six large-body requests one at a time, with a label on each, to find the failing one, and re-run the file a few times to see whether the reset is flaky or consistent.
